title: Stochastic deceleration guard for canary splits
creator: Ava Chen
body:
Background: Our current rollout engine uses deterministic step schedules and hard threshold guardrails (e.g., error_rate > X => pause/rollback). That works for many cases but is brittle for noisy traffic patterns or for models with slowly drifting quality metrics. We want a policy primitive that probabilistically throttles traffic increases based on observed metric volatility and signal confidence, reducing noisy false-positive rollbacks while still providing conservative protection when signals are strong.

Proposal: Implement a Stochastic Deceleration Guard (SDG) as part of the canary policy engine. SDG evaluates metric stability and dynamically reduces the planned step growth using a probabilistic factor. Key capabilities: 
- Volatility scoring: rolling-window stat (e.g., EWMA of variance) per metric (latency_p95, error_rate, hallucination_rate, relevance_score).
- Confidence-adjusted throttle: convert volatility and sample size into a confidence scalar in [0,1]. Lower confidence => stronger deceleration.
- Probabilistic step throttle: planned next_step_percent = planned * (1 - throttle_factor) where throttle_factor is drawn from a Beta distribution parameterized by volatility and confidence to introduce stochasticity.
- Step-back on regression: if a metric crosses a hard degradation boundary, auto-step-back to previous stable allocation and optionally trigger rollback after sustained breach.
- Shadow-aware behavior: when using shadow traffic, prefer to raise confidence from shadow signals but cap impact until shadow sample reaches minimum.
- Simulation mode + dry-run: allow policy to be evaluated in the simulator against historical traces before enabling in production.

Config sketch (example canary policy fragment):

policy:
  type: staged
  steps:
    - percent: 5
      duration: 10m
    - percent: 20
      duration: 20m
    - percent: 50
      duration: 30m
  guards:
    - type: stochastic_deceleration
      metrics: ["latency_p95", "error_rate", "semantic_relevance"]
      window: 15m
      min_samples: 200
      max_throttle: 0.7          # never reduce growth by more than 70%
      beta_alpha_scale: 1.5     # tuning param for Beta distribution
      hard_thresholds:
        error_rate: 0.02        # immediate step-back if crossed
        latency_p95: 800        # ms
      step_back_duration: 15m
      evaluation_interval: 1m

Decision trade-offs considered:
- Deterministic vs probabilistic: deterministic deceleration was simpler but led to oscillation on noisy metrics; stochasticity reduces synchronized behavior across rollouts and avoids deterministic patterns attackers could exploit.
- Complexity vs safety: SDG adds complexity to policy evaluation and introduces randomness; mitigations include simulation mode, observability, conservative defaults, and opt-in per-customer.
- Performance: metric scoring and sampling must be cheap; implement with streaming EWMA calculators and approximate counters rather than heavy queries.

Implementation plan:
1) Design: finalize volatility/confidence formulas and Beta parameterization (Owner: Marcus). Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUN/SDG+Design
2) Simulator: extend rollout simulator to replay traces and apply SDG decisions (Owner: Leah). Unit & integration tests with synthetic noise profiles.
3) Runtime: implement SDG evaluator in policy engine (Owner: Marcus, Reviewer: Diego Ramos). Evaluate performance overhead in canary hot path; add caching and evaluation budget.
4) Observability: dashboards for throttle factor distribution, metric volatility, step-back events, and false-positive rate. Alert on unexpected throttling.
5) Beta: enable opt-in for Dedicated customers and internal rollout team. Monitor for 2 weeks, iterate on tunables.

Acceptance criteria:
- SDG can be enabled as a guard in canary policies and exposes tunables in policy schema.
- Simulator shows reduced rollback frequency on noisy traffic traces without increasing customer-impactful degradations.
- Runtime CPU overhead for policy evaluation < 3% at 10k TPS control plane evaluations (target).
- Documentation and runbook published in Confluence.

Risks / Mitigations:
- Non-deterministic behavior complicates debugging: add correlation IDs, deterministic seed option for replay.
- Tuning risk: expose conservative defaults and require opt-in per organization.
- Metric poisoning: combine multiple orthogonal signals and require hard_thresholds for immediate protections.

Rollout steps:
- Internal dry-run (simulator) -> internal canary on low-risk customers -> beta customers -> enable as default for new policies in runtime-1.24 release.

2026-03-12 - Diego Ramos: Code review done; requested benchmark and additional test for shadow traffic sample ramp. Marcus addressing comments.
